findings.issue: String-prefix parent containment admitted profile-internal leaf ..payload. Actual output now checks exact first relative path component .. before admission.
Cached unchanged map could skip original control CAS at checkpoint. Actual mapped flush now invokes per-file OriginalControl::load and latches failure even with unchanged map bytes.
Compact conversion device/inode were cast to signed original journal without range gate. Actual output now checks both fit int64 before persisting intent.
Deprecated filelinks has no actual original reader; AT_FILE_LINKS2 exclusively drives getFileLinksSupport. Preserve filelinks opaque rather than treating it as authority.

Original DiskManagerImpl completion strips incomplete suffix on linked names and strips unskipped dnd_pfx. Current native completion preserves absolute external names and does not strip dnd_pfx. Logical IO can remain compatible, but exact completion-name parity is not established for those inputs.

integrate.py is a one-shot transformation over baseline copied inputs. It is not idempotent and no longer reproduces all reviewed manual corrections; do not rerun it over adopted/current sources or describe it as final runtime replay recipe.

proof_notes: C+intent before/after expansion retains packed source edge; state L is saved before retiring both original primary/backup controls; intent is cleared only afterward. Replaying L+intent after either retirement boundary avoids recopying unrelated data.

Journal index/format/dev/inode are validated against current authenticated payload before mutation. No missing mapping is promoted to a verified resume state; prepare persists all RECHECK flags first.
Explicit filelinks2 resolves to held nofollow descriptors; external physical names are retained in original links, padding stays virtual, same-path/inode aliases are rejected.

Completion controls use separate fixed-name original resilient candidates, whole observed stamp validation, same-directory sync and retained failure candidates. This source review is not a power-loss or runtime proof.
